title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 448
paragraphs: Having driven him out, he asked the elder son what their mother's father had said to them in his conversation. He related how Procles had received them kindly, but of the saying he had uttered when parting from them he had no memory, since he had taken no note of it. So Periander said that it could not be that Procles had not suggested something to them, and he pressed him with further questions; and after that he remembered, and told of this too. Then Periander, taking note of it and not wishing to show any indulgence, sent a messenger to those with whom the son who had been driven out was staying at that time and forbade them to receive him into their houses. Whenever, having been driven from one house, he came to another, he was driven away from this one too, since Periander threatened those who received him and commanded them to turn him out; and so, being driven away again, he would go to another house where friends of his lived, and they perhaps received him because he was Periander's son, even though they feared.
